title: Eighteen Hours
subtitle: Rising Crest, Evacuation Clock & Levee Fight

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday 20 April 2027, after a wet April. The exercise starts at 06:00 with TCEMA (Coordinator Marcus Ellery, Deputy Hannah Brandvold, PIO Josie Pruitt) in Monitoring: the Cedar River at Cedar Ford (CFDI4) reads 12.4 ft and a flood warning is in effect with a forecast crest of 18.2 ft (minor) on Friday at 06:00. The categories are action 13.0, flood 15.0, moderate 19.0, major 23.0; the levee design flood is 25.5 ft and the levee crest 26.0 ft. At 18:00 Tuesday the River Forecast Center revises the crest to 21.8 ft (moderate) on Friday at 20:00 after 2.4 inches of rain in the upper basin; at 12:00 Wednesday a further revision gives 23.4 ft (major) on Saturday at 06:00, and the stage reaches 19.0 ft on Thursday at 14:00. Pressure points: Cedar Hollow (about 140 homes, 22 medical-needs households, Hollow Court Care Center with 36 beds and a 12-hour clearance) floods at 19.0 ft so the mandatory order must be given at least 18 hours before that stage, and the first revision does not require it while the second one does, with the deadline at Wednesday 20:00; TallisAlert voice calls take 25 minutes; River Road closes at 15.0 ft, the Mill Street underpass at 17.0, Route 38 bottoms at 19.0 and Hollow Road at 19.5, and Iowa DOT closes the Route 38 bridge at 24.5 ft or for scour; the Levee and Drainage District No. 3 (Superintendent Bill Hoeksema) holds 40,000 of the 80,000 sandbags it needs and 2 of 6 pumps and Pump Station 1 has 36 hours of fuel; Friday at 08:00 a patrol reports a sand boil with muddy water near the Hollow Creek low spot (station 18+50) at 22.0 ft; a post says the levee has failed; Tallis Prairie Cooperative needs 24 hours to move 340 cattle and secure anhydrous ammonia tanks; the Cedar Ford Wastewater Treatment Plant must decide whether to bypass at 24.0 ft and notify the Iowa Department of Natural Resources; Cedar Ford High School opens as a shelter with a pet area; Tallis Elementary closes; Iowa HSEMD is asked for bags, pumps and a declaration. Decisions the exercise should record: EOC activation level with the basis, evacuation advisory and order with clearance time, road closures with the stage that floods them, sandbag and pump orders with needed-by times, shelter opening, moves of stock and facilities, request for state help, public messages with the category stated. The SimCell plays the National Weather Service forecast office and River Forecast Center, the USGS gauge staff, the Army Corps of Engineers, Iowa DOT, Iowa HSEMD, the Red Cross, the care center administrator, the cooperative manager, the downstream county, reporters and residents.
constraints: Every county email address uses the exercise domain tallisco-ia.example; the levee district uses leveed3.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

NWS products follow the real format: flood warnings name the river point, category, forecast crest with time and impacts; stages are in feet at CFDI4; revised forecasts say what changed; a flash flood tag is not used for a river flood; times are Central Daylight Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the National Weather Service, River Forecast Center, USGS, Army Corps of Engineers, Iowa DOT, Iowa HSEMD, the Red Cross, the care center, the cooperative, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Making decisions on the latest forecast issuance before the lead time runs out, flood-fighting a levee with half the resources the plan needs, and keeping the public message tied to the measured stage and the right flood category.
overview.threat: After a wet April, the Cedar River at Cedar Ford (CFDI4) is rising toward a spring flood. At STARTEX, 06:00 Tuesday 20 April 2027, the gauge reads 12.4 ft and a flood warning forecasts a minor crest of 18.2 ft at 06:00 Friday. After 2.4 inches of rain in the upper basin, the River Forecast Center raises the crest at 18:00 Tuesday to 21.8 ft (moderate) at 20:00 Friday. At 12:00 Wednesday it raises it again to 23.4 ft (major) at 06:00 Saturday, with the river reaching 19.0 ft at 14:00 Thursday. Cedar Hollow, the roads and crossings in the river reach, Pump Stations 1 and 2, the Levee and Drainage District No. 3 earthen levee and its Hollow Creek low spot, and the Cedar Ford Wastewater Treatment Plant behind the levee all come under threat.
overview.operationalImpact: The second revision leaves only eight hours, until 20:00 Wednesday, to issue the mandatory Cedar Hollow order. The order has to go out at least 18 hours before the river reaches 19.0 ft so the 12-hour clearance can finish in time. About 140 homes and 22 medical-needs households need door-to-door contact from deputies and Cedar Ford Fire. Hollow Court Care Center has to move 36 residents by van and paratransit bus, and Hollow Road becomes one-way outbound. TallisAlert voice calls take 25 minutes county-wide, so the PIO has to word each message with the correct category while residents and reporters call. Public Works has to close River Road at 15.0 ft, the Mill Street underpass at 17.0 ft, Route 38 bottoms at 19.0 ft and Hollow Road at 19.5 ft before the water reaches them. Motorists and farm families lose their routes, and Iowa DOT may close the Route 38 bridge at 24.5 ft or for scour. The Levee District has 40,000 of the 80,000 sandbags and 2 of the 6 pumps it needs, and Pump Station 1 has only 36 hours of fuel. Patrols move to around the clock. At 08:00 Friday, with the river at 22.0 ft, a patrol reports a sand boil carrying muddy water near station 18+50 at the Hollow Creek low spot. Within minutes, a social media post falsely claims the levee has failed, and 911 lines fill with calls from the 340 homes behind it. Tallis Prairie Cooperative needs 24 hours to move 340 cattle and secure its anhydrous ammonia tanks. The wastewater plant has to move chemicals and its generator above 24.0 ft and decide whether to bypass at 24.0 ft, which means notifying the Iowa Department of Natural Resources. Tallis Elementary closes, Cedar Ford High School opens as a shelter with a pet area, and Iowa HSEMD is asked for bags, pumps and a disaster declaration.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to set the EOC activation level and issue the mandatory Cedar Hollow evacuation order by 20:00 Wednesday, at least 18 hours before the river reaches 19.0 ft at CFDI4, and to name the River Forecast Center issuance and the gauge reading each decision is based on.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to send TallisAlert, website, radio and door-to-door messages that use the correct CFDI4 flood category and the latest forecast crest and time, state the old and new numbers when the forecast is revised, and answer the false levee-failure post from the rumor log within 20 minutes.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to carry out the stage triggers in the Levee District plan and the County EOP: close River Road, the Mill Street underpass, Route 38 bottoms and Hollow Road before the water reaches them, increase levee patrols, and report the district's judgement of the levee's condition once the forecast crest reaches 23.0 ft.

objectives.name: Infrastructure Protection
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to protect Pump Station 1 and the Cedar Ford Wastewater Treatment Plant: order diesel fuel at least 12 hours before the tank falls below one half, decide the 24.0 ft bypass with notice to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources, and send the sand boil at station 18+50 up through the EOC to the Army Corps of Engineers and Iowa HSEMD as resource requests.

roles.name: TCEMA Coordinator (EOC Command / Incident Commander)
roles.team: Team A: EM Coordinator / EOC Command
roles.description: Owns the EOC activation level, the evacuation orders, shelter opening, requests to Iowa HSEMD for resources and a disaster declaration, and the final call on public warnings.
standingOrders: Latest Issuance: base every decision on the most recent River Forecast Center issuance, and record the issuance, the gauge reading or the report you used.
Clock Before Crest: count back from the time the river reaches 19.0 ft at CFDI4, not from the crest. The Cedar Hollow order goes out 18 hours ahead even if the forecast may change again.
Single Voice: all public statements go through the PIO, and all outside requests go through the EOC. No position acts alone with the state or the media.
Field Over Screen: when a patrol report and the gauge feed disagree, act on the field report and verify afterward.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns all public messages on TallisAlert, the county website, Facebook and local radio, checking that the county, city, Levee District and Red Cross messages agree, and keeping the rumor log.
standingOrders: Category Discipline: never call a stage minor, moderate or major unless the CFDI4 category table says so, and always give the forecast crest with its time and issuance.
Truth Over Reassurance: when the forecast is revised, say "The forecast crest has been revised" and give the old and new numbers. Do not soften a major forecast to calm callers.
Rumor Clock: answer a levee-break or shelter rumor from the rumor log within 20 minutes, using only facts the Levee Superintendent has confirmed.
WEA Discipline: use a Wireless Emergency Alert only for a mandatory evacuation order, never for a river stage advisory.

roles.name: Levee and Drainage District No. 3 Superintendent (Levee District)
roles.description: Owns the flood fight on the 3.8-mile levee: patrols, sandbagging, sand boils and seepage, the Hollow Creek low spot and gated outlet, and Pump Stations 1 and 2.
standingOrders: Trigger Discipline: increase patrols, gate closures and sandbag rings at the stage triggers in the district plan, not by the clock or on gut feel.
Report Early: tell the Coordinator about any boil, seepage or slide at once, with the station number, and do not wait until you have the full picture.
Fuel Ahead: order Pump Station 1 diesel through county Logistics at least 12 hours before the tank falls below one half.
Honest Judgement: at each briefing once the forecast crest is at or above 23.0 ft, give your judgement of the levee's condition, even if it is bad news.

roles.name: Sheriff and Cedar Ford Fire Chief (Sheriff and Fire Field Operations)
roles.team: Team D: Sheriff and Fire Field Operations
roles.description: Manages door-to-door evacuation notices, the 22 medical-needs households, traffic control on outbound Hollow Road, 911 call surges and swift water rescue readiness.
standingOrders: Safety First: do not send crews or residents onto roads or crossings that are flooding. If dispatch and the field disagree, trust the field.
Knock Every Door: record contact with every Cedar Hollow home and every medical-needs household, and report anyone who refuses to leave or cannot be reached.
Verify Before Responding: send a unit to confirm any reported levee failure before you start a mass response, and pass what it finds to the EOC right away.

roles.name: Public Works Director
roles.description: Owns road and crossing closures, barricades and variable message signs, the Hollow Road one-way detour, county pumps and the coordination with the Iowa DOT liaison on Route 38.
standingOrders: Close Before Water: close River Road at 15.0 ft, the Mill Street underpass at 17.0 ft, Route 38 bottoms at 19.0 ft and Hollow Road at 19.5 ft before the water reaches them, even if motorists complain.
Routes Matter: keep an evacuation route and a supply route open to the levee, the wastewater plant and the shelter, and tell the EOC before you cut any route.
Report Status: give every closure the road name, its status, the stage at which it floods and the time, so the PIO can publish it.

roles.name: Cedar Ford Wastewater Treatment Plant Superintendent
roles.description: Manages plant operations behind the levee: moving chemicals and the generator above 24.0 ft, keeping the access road usable, the bypass decision and the notice to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources.
standingOrders: Protect Early: move chemicals and the generator above 24.0 ft while the access road is still open, before the river reaches 19.0 ft.
Continuity vs. Containment: keep treating as long as it is safe, but decide on bypass at 24.0 ft based on the stage and the forecast, not on hope.
Notify Through EOC: report a bypass to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources as the plan requires, and tell the Coordinator and the PIO first so the public message matches.

phases.title: The Rising Watch
phases.goal: Tests whether the EOC and the Levee District act early on an uncertain minor forecast: setting the activation level, starting action-stage measures and ordering sandbags and pumps before the lead time runs out. Also tests whether they recognize the first forecast revision and act on it.
beats: STARTEX (Tue 06:00): an exercise-marked NWS flood warning for the Cedar River at Cedar Ford (CFDI4) gives a gauge reading of 12.4 ft and a forecast crest of 18.2 ft at 06:00 Friday. That is minor flooding under the EOP 2 category table (above the 15.0 ft flood stage, below the 19.0 ft moderate category). It lists the minor impacts: Riverside Park, River Road south of Mill Street and Water Street basements. The TCEMA Coordinator has to set the EOC activation level and name the issuance it rests on.

Action-stage squeeze: the river is 0.6 ft below the 13.0 ft action stage. Under Levee District Plan 3, that stage triggers the Superintendent's call to the county, daily inspections and opening the fill station at the district shop. EOP 6.3 asks for sandbag and pump orders to Iowa HSEMD 24 hours before action stage, so that window has already closed. The district holds 40,000 of the 80,000 bags the plan needs and 2 of the 6 pumps, which leaves the shortfall to be requested through the EOC as an ICS 213 general message.
Noise item: a routine USGS notice about scheduled maintenance on a different, upstream gauge. Players should note it and set it aside.

First schedule question: the Tallis Elementary principal and Tallis Prairie Cooperative (SimCell) ask whether to change plans. The cooperative says it needs 24 hours to move 340 cattle and secure its anhydrous ammonia tanks, and asks what stage and time it should plan for.

Time jump (Tue 18:00): after 2.4 inches of rain in the upper basin, the River Forecast Center revises the crest to 21.8 ft (moderate) at 20:00 Friday. That is more than 36 hours out and at or above 19.0 ft, so it meets the EOP 6.1 trigger for a voluntary Cedar Hollow evacuation advisory. The PIO has to send the TallisAlert and Tallis Valley Radio messages with the old and new crests (18.2 ft and 21.8 ft) and the new category.

phases.title: Water in the Streets
phases.goal: Tests whether Public Works closes roads before they flood on a stated stage, and whether the PIO and EOC keep the public picture tied to the latest issuance and the measured CFDI4 stage while partners press for resources.
beats: Time jump (Wed 07:00): CFDI4 reads 14.8 ft and is rising. Public Works has to place barricades on River Road south of Mill Street before it floods at 15.0 ft (SFMECS 4), give the closure basis and stage, and issue a closure notice. The City of Cedar Ford has to plan the Mill Street underpass closure at 17.0 ft. First field reports come in of water in Riverside Park and Water Street basements.

Red herring: a resident calls 911 to report that the Hollow Creek gated outlet is stuck open and the river is backing into the ditch system. The Levee District patrol checks and finds the gate closed and working; the water is rain ponding in a field. Players should check before they react.

Stale forecast trap: a Tallis Valley Radio reporter (SimCell) has a noon deadline and quotes the Tuesday morning 18.2 ft minor crest. Social media is repeating the same figure. The PIO has to correct the record with the 18:00 Tuesday issuance (21.8 ft, moderate, 20:00 Friday) and say what changed.
Visual confirmation: a Levee District patrol photo shows the CFDI4 staff gauge on the Route 38 bridge piers, with the reading and the time. A screenshot of the USGS reading is shown next to it.

Partner request: Hollow Court Care Center (SimCell) asks the EOC to commit eight vans and a paratransit bus now. It needs 12 hours to move its 36 residents and wants to know whether the advisory will become an order. The Coordinator has to decide whether to commit them now or hold.
Time jump (Wed 12:00): the River Forecast Center issues a second revision with a crest of 23.4 ft (major) at 06:00 Saturday. The river is now forecast to reach 19.0 ft at 14:00 Thursday.

phases.title: The Eighteen-Hour Clock
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's single decision point: issuing the mandatory Cedar Hollow evacuation order by 20:00 Wednesday on the 12:00 issuance, at a real cost either way. It also tests mass care, the state request and the levee condition report triggered by a major crest.
beats: DECISION POINT (Wed 12:00–20:00): under EOP 6.1, the mandatory order for Cedar Hollow has to go out by 20:00 Wednesday, 18 hours before the river reaches 19.0 ft at 14:00 Thursday, so the 12-hour clearance finishes 6 hours ahead of the water. Ordering now moves about 140 homes, 22 medical-needs households and the 36 Hollow Court Care Center residents on a forecast that could still change. Waiting for a clearer forecast puts that clearance time at risk. The Coordinator has to state the RFC issuance and the gauge reading the decision rests on.

Execution: deputies and Cedar Ford Fire carry out door-to-door contact using the SFMECS 3 Cedar Hollow procedure. Hollow Road becomes one-way outbound. The care center vans and paratransit bus need staging. Tallis Elementary closes, and Cedar Ford High School opens as a shelter with the pet area, with the Red Cross and the school district deciding staffing (EOP 6.4). A medical-needs household refuses to leave, and a deputy reports that two shift staff cannot get in from across the river.

Major-crest triggers: the forecast crest of 23.4 ft is at or above 23.0 ft. Under EOP 6.6 the county requests a disaster declaration from Iowa HSEMD, along with the missing 40,000 bags and four 6-inch pumps. Under Levee District Plan 3, the Superintendent has to give the district's judgement of the levee's condition, including the Hollow Creek low spot that sits 1.1 ft lower than the rest, at the next EOC briefing.

Time jump (Wed 22:00, 17.0 ft): the city closes the Mill Street underpass and the district closes the pump station gates. The PUD feeder to Pump Station 1 at Mill Street is lost, so the Assistant Superintendent switches to diesel and the 36-hour fuel clock starts. Under Levee District Plan 6, the fuel order has to reach the county Logistics position at least 12 hours before the tank falls below one half.

Public information deadline: the TallisAlert voice call takes 25 minutes county-wide. The PIO has to word the order with the major category, the 23.4 ft crest at 06:00 Saturday and the change from 21.8 ft. A rumor that 'the whole south side must leave tonight' has to be countered with the right area (Cedar Hollow, not the 340 leveed homes). Public Works plans the Route 38 bottoms closure at 19.0 ft with Iowa DOT and the Hollow Road closure at 19.5 ft.

phases.title: Boil, Bypass, Return
phases.goal: Tests the flood fight and infrastructure protection at the crest: escalating the sand boil, answering the levee-failure rumor within 20 minutes and making the wastewater plant bypass call. It then tests damage assessment and a phased return to service.
beats: Time jump (Fri 08:00, 22.0 ft): a two-person foot patrol on the 24-hour rotation reports a sand boil carrying muddy water near station 18+50 at the Hollow Creek low spot, using a levee patrol field report. Under Levee District Plan 3, the 22.0 ft actions include sandbag rings, closing Levee Road to the public and an Army Corps of Engineers technical assistance request. The EOC has to send these up to the Corps and Iowa HSEMD as resource requests. If the stage approaches 24.0 ft, the 18-hour evacuation clock for the 340 leveed homes has to be raised with the Coordinator.

Within minutes, a social media post falsely claims the levee has failed. The 911 lines at the Communications Center fill with calls from the 340 homes behind the levee. The PIO has to log the rumor and put out a correction tied to the measured CFDI4 stage and the patrol report within 20 minutes.

Wastewater plant: seepage and interior ponding reach the yard because the pump stations are falling behind at the 22.5 ft equivalent, and the SCADA room floor sits at that level. Under TCCFFS 4, the Plant Superintendent has to move the chemical totes, portable pumps and the mobile generator above 24.0 ft and decide whether to shut down and bypass at 24.0 ft. A bypass sends untreated flow to the river and requires notifying the Iowa Department of Natural Resources.

Hurdle: the diesel delivery to Pump Station 1 is delayed because Levee Road and Route 38 bottoms are closed. Separately, Iowa DOT warns that it may close the Route 38 Cedar Ford Bridge for scour inspection. The Coordinator and Public Works have to find another route and set restoration priorities between the pump stations and the plant.

Time jump (Sat afternoon): the river crests near the 23.4 ft forecast and starts to fall. Players carry out damage assessment in Cedar Hollow and on the levee, inspect closed roads before reopening (SFMECS 4), plan a phased return for Cedar Hollow residents and Hollow Court Care Center, and make final notifications to Iowa HSEMD, Iowa DNR and the Corps. Then ENDEX.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The TCEMA Coordinator has to turn the forecasts into the EOP 6 decisions on time. That means the voluntary advisory, the mandatory Cedar Hollow order by 20:00 Wednesday, opening the shelter, and the requests to Iowa HSEMD, all worked out with the Sheriff and Fire, Hollow Court and the Red Cross.

Under SFMECS 2, each decision has to rest on a named River Forecast Center issuance and a CFDI4 gauge reading. Players record each issuance on the River Status Board, spot a material revision, and decide on time instead of waiting for a better forecast.

The PIO has to send TallisAlert, website, radio and door-to-door messages that use the correct CFDI4 category and the latest crest. When the forecast is revised, the messages give the old and new numbers. The PIO also uses the WEA only for an order and answers the levee-failure rumors from the rumor log within 20 minutes (EOP 7, SFMECS 8).

Public Works, the City and Iowa DOT have to close River Road, the Mill Street underpass, Route 38 bottoms and Hollow Road at the SFMECS 4 stages, before the water reaches each road. Each closure needs a recorded basis, and no road reopens until it has been inspected.

The EOP 6 stage triggers include requesting state help when the forecast crest reaches 23.0 ft or the levee shows distress. That request depends on the Levee District reporting the levee's condition to the EOC.

Pump Station 1 has to keep running on diesel after the feeder is lost, with fuel ordered in time under Levee District Plan 6. The wastewater plant has to move its chemicals and generator above 24.0 ft before the access road floods (EOP 6.5).
The sand boil and the shortfall in bags and pumps have to go up through the EOC as requests to Iowa HSEMD for resources and state help, as EOP 6.3 and 6.6 require.

questions.text: At I-11 (14:12–14:18 Wednesday), the hydrologist told you the 23.4 ft crest was ±1.5 ft and 19.0 ft could come as early as 10:00 Thursday. Then the Hollow Court Care Center administrator gave you until 15:00 to lock in Meadowview and the vans. Did you order the Cedar Hollow evacuation then, or did you wait for the 18:00 issuance? Which issuance and gauge reading did you write down as the basis, as SFMECS 3 requires? How did you weigh the care center's 12-hour start time against the cost of a false alarm? At I-06, Patrol L-1 sent a staff-gauge photo reading about 14.9 ft at 07:17, while the USGS page was stuck at 14.81 ft from 07:00. From I-04b through I-07 and I-11b, the public heard three numbers: '20 feet already', the TV and radio's stale 18.2 ft minor crest, and 'whole south side out by midnight.' What did you tell the Tallis Valley Radio reporter before the 11:30 and 15:00 deadlines? Did your messages name the latest crest, its time, its category and the old and new numbers? Did you make clear that the order covered Cedar Hollow only and not everyone behind the levee? Did you answer each rumor within 20 minutes?

At I-12, the plan met the street. The man on oxygen at house 14 would not leave his dog. Two medical-needs households didn't answer. The Hollow Court night aides were stuck behind the one-way barrier on Hollow Road. Red Cross couldn't open the pet area before 19:00. Who in the EOC owned each of those problems? Did operations and the care center understand each other's limits? What would you change in SFMECS 3 steps 3–5 so that traffic control doesn't block the people the evacuation depends on?

At I-15b, a video claimed the levee broke at Hollow Creek, and 911 took 61 calls in nine minutes with no confirmation. How long did it take the Levee District patrol to confirm or deny it? What did you give the 911 call-takers to tell callers? Had the district already reported its judgement of the levee's condition once the forecast crest reached 23.0 ft? And did the sand boil at station 18+50 and the Pump Station 1 fuel order go up through the EOC to the Army Corps of Engineers and Iowa HSEMD as resource requests, or stay inside the district?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: NWS Quad Cities forecast office (DVN) hydrologist, speaking also for the North Central River Forecast Center forecast for CFDI4
simcellScripts.trigger: Any player calls or messages the Weather Service to ask what the CFDI4 forecast means, whether the crest will change, or when 19.0 ft will be reached, most likely after I-04, I-09 or during I-11.
hardQuestions: Which issuance are you working from? The 06:00 Tuesday product is two forecasts old. If you're quoting 18.2 ft, you're quoting a dead number.

What decisions are you trying to make, and at what stage? Tell me your thresholds, like 19.0 ft for Cedar Hollow and 24.0 ft for the plant, and I'll give you timing against those. I can't tell you whether to evacuate.

The crest is 23.4 ft, give or take 1.5 ft, and 19.0 ft arrives at 14:00 Thursday, give or take 4 hours, with the early side more likely. If you wait for the 18:00 issuance, does your 18-hour clock still work?
Who's checking the gauge? The USGS page for CFDI4 is provisional and hasn't updated since 07:00. Do you have eyes on the staff gauge?
concessions: If the EOC gives its decision thresholds and asks for decision support, the hydrologist gives timing for each stage the county named and holds a short IDSS call with the EOC at each new issuance.

If the PIO asks, the hydrologist confirms which flood category the current product states, so county messages can use the same category. The hydrologist will not give the county a category of its own.
If the players ask about the upstream gauge (I-01b), the hydrologist confirms that the Gauge 2 maintenance gap does not affect CFDI4, and that missing upstream data does not mean zero flow.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: City of Cedar Ford, City Administrator Fran Oyelaran, speaking for the city's emergency management and street crew
simcellScripts.trigger: Team A or Team E contacts the city about closing the Mill Street underpass, about Water Street basements, or about a joint public message, or does not answer the city's text in I-05.
hardQuestions: I've got four barricades and a two-man crew. What stage are we closing Mill Street on, and who's signing it? I'm not closing a state-funded underpass on a guess.
You closed River Road at 07:30. Did you close it before the water got there, or after a commuter drove through it?
Water Street people are calling me, not you. Is the city saying minor, moderate or major? Your radio interview and my Facebook page had better use the same number.
If Cedar Hollow goes mandatory, is the city's name on that order or just the county's? My council will ask.
concessions: If the EOC gives a written closure basis tied to a stage, such as 17.0 ft at CFDI4 per SFMECS 4, the city closes the Mill Street underpass on that stage and reports the time it closed.
If the PIO sends the city an approved message with the current issuance and category, the city posts it word for word on its own channels.
If Public Works confirms who will inspect the underpass before reopening, the city agrees not to reopen it on its own.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Iowa Homeland Security and Emergency Management (HSEMD) regional duty officer
simcellScripts.trigger: Team A or Team C asks the state for sandbags, pumps, Guard sandbag crews or a disaster declaration, most likely around I-13 or earlier if players think ahead.
hardQuestions: What exactly do you need: how many bags, how many 6-inch pumps, delivered where and needed by when? "As many as you can" goes to the bottom of the pile.
Is it in WebEOC? I can't move anything off a phone call. And I need your declaration request by 18:00 if you want to be on tonight's proclamation.
Where's the district's written statement on the levee's condition? No statement, no Guard crews.
What have you already used locally? Have you exhausted your own sand, bags and contractors, or am I your first call?
concessions: Once a WebEOC request names the resource, quantity, delivery point (for example, the district shop) and a needed-by time, the duty officer gives an estimated arrival time for the 40,000 bags and four pumps.
Once the Superintendent submits the written levee condition statement, Tallis is added to the list for Guard sandbag crews.
Once the declaration request is in by 18:00, Tallis County is included in the Governor's proclamation package.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: US Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island District, levee safety and geotechnical engineer
simcellScripts.trigger: Team C requests a technical assistance visit (Levee District plan, section 3, at 22.0 ft) or answers the I-13 email, or calls the Corps about the sand boil at station 18+50 in I-15.
hardQuestions: Who's asking? I need the request from the district as the levee sponsor, not from someone who heard about the levee secondhand.
Give me the boil the way your patrol logged it: station number, distance from the toe, clear or muddy, size, flow, and the stage at the time. "There's a leak" doesn't help me.
At the Hollow Creek low spot you're 1.1 ft lower than the rest of the crown. What is your freeboard there right now, and who is standing on it continuously?
Is the boil ringed? To what height? If you sealed it off, you just pushed the problem somewhere else.
concessions: Once the district formally requests the inspection, a geotechnical engineer is on site the next morning, or at once after a muddy boil is reported with a logged station and stage.

Once the patrol log is read back with the station, stage and boil description, the engineer advises ringing the boil to a height that slows the flow without sealing it, and watching the clear wet spot near 18+70.
After the crest, the engineer agrees to a written post-flood inspection recommendation for the Hollow Creek reach, which the declaration package can use.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Iowa Department of Natural Resources, wastewater field office duty staff
simcellScripts.trigger: Team F calls Iowa DNR about protecting the Cedar Ford Wastewater Treatment Plant or a possible shutdown and bypass at 24.0 ft (TCCFFS 4), or replies to the automated eDMR reminder (I-13b).
hardQuestions: Are you telling me a bypass is happening, or that it might happen? Give me the start time, or the stage you'll start at, and how much flow is going untreated to the river.
Who's downstream of your outfall? Have downstream communities and water users been told?
Where are your hypo and bisulfite totes right now? If they're still on the low pad and the yard floods, that's a second report.
(If they bring up the eDMR) That's the compliance desk's automated reminder. I'm not the one to call about March paperwork. Tell me about this week.
concessions: Once the plant gives a stage-based plan with an estimated start time and the outfall location, DNR accepts a verbal notice now with a written follow-up.
Once the chemicals and generator are confirmed moved above 24.0 ft, DNR records the plant's protective actions in the file.
If the plant bypasses, DNR asks for a sampling plan and a return-to-service notice. DNR will discuss flexibility on the March eDMR deadline only after the bypass notice is on record.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. The aim is to test the Tallis County EOP, the Levee and Drainage District No. 3 flood fight plan and the EOC communications procedures, not to judge any person, agency or department.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. The CFDI4 gauge readings, the River Forecast Center issuances and the field reports are the facts players have to work with. Do not argue the scenario. Act on it.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the County EOP stage table, activation levels and lead times, and the Levee District roles and stage triggers. Where a plan is silent, players say so and state the decision they would make.
Each decision names the forecast issuance and the CFDI4 gauge reading it is based on, the same way it would be logged in the EOC.
Decisions and actions from earlier modules carry forward, even when a time jump skips how they were carried out.
Players speak for their own position. Anything outside the room goes through the SimCell.
artificialities: Time jumps compress about four days of flooding (Tuesday 20 April to Saturday 24 April 2027) into four one-hour modules. Exercise clock times and scenario times are different and are shown on each card.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room: the NWS Quad Cities office and the North Central River Forecast Center, USGS, Iowa HSEMD, Iowa DOT, Iowa DNR, the Army Corps of Engineers (Rock Island District), the Red Cross, the City of Cedar Ford, Hollow Court Care Center, the receiving care home, the cooperative, the media, the utility, the fuel contractor, 911 callers and residents.

TallisAlert, IPAWS, WebEOC, the county website, the USGS real-time page and the Levee District radios are named as they appear in the plans but are not used. Players say what they would send and to whom, and no real message goes out.
Injects, including NWS products marked TEST, social media posts, emails, radio calls and CAD entries, are delivered on paper or on screen. No real public post or alert is created.
Field work such as closing roads, bagging, patrols, evacuations and moving equipment is described rather than carried out, and is assumed to take realistic time and staff.

**Module 1: The Rising Watch.** Exercise clock 06:00–07:00. The scenario runs from Tuesday 20 April 2027 at 06:00 through Tuesday evening.

It is 06:00 CDT on Tuesday 20 April 2027, after the wettest April in years. It is overcast with light rain, 48°F, wind SE 10 mph. TCEMA is in Monitoring. The Coordinator and the Levee Superintendent are checking in by phone, one deputy is staffing the EOC at the Courthouse annex, and the PIO is on the way in. No roads are closed, Pump Stations 1 and 2 are idle, the wastewater plant is treating normal flow and schools are open.

The duty officer hands you the 05:15 NWS Quad Cities Flood Warning for the Cedar River at Cedar Ford (CFDI4). The stage was 12.4 ft at 05:00, against an action stage of 13.0 ft and a flood stage of 15.0 ft. The river is forecast to rise above flood stage late Wednesday and crest near 18.2 ft at 06:00 Friday, which is **minor flooding**. The listed impacts are Riverside Park, River Road south of Mill Street and Water Street basements at 15.0 ft, and the Mill Street underpass at 17.0 ft. Expect field reports, calls from partners and the next forecast cycle during this module.
keyIssues: What activation level do the 05:15 issuance and the 12.4 ft reading support, and what will you record as the basis?
The district holds 40,000 of the 80,000 sandbags the flood fight plan needs and 2 of the 6 pumps. The order lead time is tied to action stage, which the river may reach this afternoon.
Partners, including the cooperative, the school and the media, want a stage and a time they can plan on while the forecast is still uncertain.
There are not enough barricades for both River Road and the Mill Street underpass, and people are gathering at the boat ramp.
If the forecast is revised during this module, how is the change recognized, logged and acted on?

**Module 4: Boil, Bypass, Return.** Exercise clock 09:00–10:00. The scenario runs from Friday 23 April 2027 at 08:00 through Saturday 24 April.

It is 08:00 CDT on Friday 23 April. CFDI4 reads 22.0 ft and is rising about 0.07 ft an hour. The forecast in force is the 12:00 Wednesday issuance, reaffirmed at 06:00 today: **major** flooding, crest near 23.4 ft at 06:00 Saturday. Cedar Hollow has been under water since Thursday afternoon, and the evacuation and the Hollow Court move went the way your Module 3 decisions set them. Route 38 bottoms and Hollow Road are closed. Pump Station 1 has run on diesel since 22:04 Wednesday. Its tank was topped up at 15:30 Thursday and now reads just above half. Two-person foot patrols are on the 24-hour rotation, and the crews are on their third straight day.

At 08:02 Team L-3 radios an emergency report from station 18+50 at the Hollow Creek low spot. There is a sand boil about 25 ft out from the landside toe, with a cone about 18 inches across. It is boiling steadily and the water is **muddy**, at about pencil-thick flow. The ground is wet out to about 10 ft, and there is a second wet spot near 18+70 that is clear so far. The crew reports no cracks or slumps on the crown. L-3 has 60 bags in the truck.
keyIssues: A muddy sand boil at the lowest reach is a sign of levee distress. It must be escalated through the EOC to USACE and Iowa HSEMD.
A false levee-failure report could swamp 911 and must be answered within 20 minutes.
Interior ponding is reaching the plant yard. The 24.0 ft bypass decision and Iowa DNR notice are coming up.
PS1 will fall below half a tank around the crest, and a diesel delivery is stuck at a road closure.
A possible Route 38 bridge closure for inspection, and requests from routine 911 calls, compete with the flood fight.
Planning for damage assessment and phased return has to start while the river is still at its crest.
